summary: Safety net that catches a crash in any part of the app and shows a recovery screen with a reload button instead of a blank page.
purpose: Stops one broken screen from taking down the whole app.
why: Likely reason: a crash in React would otherwise leave a blank page. The code does not state this directly.
how: Wraps the app's content. When a part inside it throws an error, records the failure in its state, logs the error to the console, and shows the recovery screen. The reload button clears the flag and reloads the page. When nothing has failed, it shows the content as normal.
inputs: The app's content (any screen) and any error that content throws.
outputs: Either the normal content, or the System Exception Intercepted screen with a Reload Application button.
risks: The reload button reloads the whole page, so anything held only in memory is lost. The on-screen text says local state is safely preserved, but this file does not check that. Errors are only logged to the console and not reported anywhere.
debug: Look in the browser console for the message that begins with the app name, which shows the error and the component stack. If the recovery screen keeps coming back after reload, the same error is repeating.
